Dated this the 10th day of January, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.822./2006 on the file of the IVth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thiruvanathapuram is the appellant herein.

entities.text: IVth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thiruvanathapuram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents in the O.P. are the respondents herein.

The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08.03.2006.
2.

According to the petitioner, on 08.03.2006 at about 01.30 p.m., while he was riding pillion on a motorcycle bearing Registration No.KL 01 U 8761 along Mannamkonam - Nettayam Public Road near Vattiyoorkavu Service Co-operative Bank, a Mahindra Tempo Van bearing Registration No.KL 01 M 7527, driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit against the motorcycle.
As a result of which, he was thrown on the road and sustained very serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.7,00,000/-.
The 1st and 2nd respondents remained ex-parte.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, but they also remained exparte.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A10.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,18,000/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

8. Heard Sri.R.Nikhil, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.P.K.Babu, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9.

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the notional income Sasidharan Nair vs Francis on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91398300/
2 of the petitioner fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.3,500/- is on the lower side.
The petitioner claimed a monthly income of Rs.4,500/-, but the Tribunal fixed it at Rs.3,500/-.
He was working as a Security Officer in a private firm.
He could not prove his income by adducing sufficient evidence.

In the above circumstances, in the light of a dictum laid down in the MACA NO. 2453 OF 2015 2025:KER:2117 decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], his notional income is liable to be fixed at Rs.5,500/-.
10.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner sustained serious injuries and his right leg above knee was amputated.
As per Ext.A9 - disability certificate, it can be seen that the petitioner suffered Type III B open infected fracture both bones (R) Leg U/3 with segmental bone loss and large soft tissue defect.
Ext.A9 disability certificate issued by the medical board, shows that he has a permanent physical disability of 60% and the same was accepted by the Tribunal as such.

The learned counsel submitted that even though his permanent permanent physcial disability is only 60%, his functional disability is 100% as he is unable to do any work, as his right leg above knee was amputated.

Since the right leg of the petitioner above the knee was amputated, he will not be able to do the job as security or any job and as such, his functional disability is liable to be fixed at 100% and I do accordingly.

11. Since, on the date of accident, he was aged 58 years, 10 % of his income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 9, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.6,53,400/-.

The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.50,000/- towards the head 'pain and sufferings', Rs.75,000/-
towards loss of amenities and Rs.1,900/- towards bystander expenses.
Similarly, a sum of Rs.1,000/- alone is awarded towards extra nourishment and Rs.25,000/- is alone awarded towards expenditure for fitting artificial limb, though the claim was Rs.40000/-.

Considering the fact that, in accident the right leg of the petitioner was amputated above knee and his functional disability is fixed at 100%, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the above heads are grossly inadequate.
Therefore, towards the head pain and suffering he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- and towards loss of amenities he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-.

13. Since the right leg of the petitioner above knee was amputated and his functional disability is fixed at 100%, I hold that he is eligible for bystander's expense at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per month for a period of 9 years.

Hence, compensation for bystanders expense is enhanced to Rs.5,40,000/-
(5,000x9x12).
14.
Towards the head extra nourishment, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is too meager and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Towards expenditure for fitting artificial limb, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded.

16. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
17. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.10,60,900/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent MACA NO. 2453 OF 2015 2025:KER:2117 is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.10,60,900/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Sixty Thousand Nine Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 9% per annum, (interest for enhanced compensation limited to 8%) from the date of the petition till realisation, with proportionate costs,
within a period of two months from today.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner,
excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
